author: jojobloblo
body: In the new snapshot, 14w32, they have added armor stands. You can use /summon commands to put the stands in different positions, along with the head. You can make everything but the head invisible, and set the head to look like a certain block. This means you can make it look like actual blocks are being rotated in the air (I got this from SethBlings video so I'll use his example).  You could make it look like you are firing tnt at something and the blocks are flying our in random directions, tilted like crazy. I'm here to ask whether or not, when avicus is updated, this would be a good idea for map making. You can't build blocks through the armor stands so it would be kind of awkward, but yeah, give me your opinion

replies.author: LeCobalt
replies.body:
Map Makers are divided in 3:

Redstoners: (Sethbling, Dragnoz, Sokar, Mumbo) These are the guys that basically build crazy redstone/command block stuff introducing new concepts like new currencies, lucky systems, cosmetics, etc. The basically build for adventure maps and do not focus on aesthetics that much. What they do can crash minecraft quite easily.
World Coders: (These are the guys that do most pvp maps, the ones that do outstandingly massive builds in a short period of time) These guys work with plugins and various plugins. Their build are basically for the community. None of them are widely recognized, they are just loved by the servers or communities they build for. As well as redstoners they need much practice before giving out commands into a console, that, sooner or later will create the maps you play on.
Vanilla Builders: (Both redstoners and coders start up as vanilla builders) The start building when inspired, normally from another minecraft build or real-world marvel, or just from something they dreamed through through the night. They start at first with a big kickstart, but after a while it wears off. A month later they get back on the world with a different technique, but they fail again. The finally discover about plugins or redstone and then, they just take their path.                                                                            
                         
  

 The thing I'm trying to say is that your idea could crash a 40 player server easily
